verdicts.reason: A breaks the design apart. The CTA sits at the top above a tiny headline. The four list items are scattered around the can, out of order and far from their bullets. The Solstice logo is shrunk to an unreadable pill in the bottom corner, and the legal line is set as large as the body copy. B keeps the original structure and reading order, but it is just the original scaled down: the CTA label, list copy and logo are too small to read at 300x250, the content sits in a narrow column, and the bottom third is dead space.

Both are unusable. Their list items are scattered and out of sequence, and neither has a clear hierarchy. A's prominent CTA and top-placed headline are its only real merits. Its logo is microscopic and its legal line is oversized. B is worse: the legal text is promoted to the top-left, the CTA is a tiny pill in the top-right, and the headline is pushed to the middle-right below the fourth list item. The supporting line is mixed in among the list items, and the logo floats alone at the bottom-right.
